# Pilot local LLM response-quality judging with selective pairwise ranking

::: {.hub-record-hero .hub-idea-hero}
<p class="hub-idea-status">Idea · High priority · 2/9 readiness fields complete</p>

<p class="hub-takeaway">Use a local judge to estimate which candidate responses are correct and useful, then compare only close or uncertain candidates.</p>
<p>Response quality could add evidence that query similarity and candidate profiles miss, but generated references and local judges can both be wrong.</p>

<p class="hub-github-issue"><a href="https://github.com/npatta01/trec_mlm_2026/issues/31">Track in GitHub #31</a></p>

<p class="hub-next-action">Freeze the pilot sample, judge schemas, acceptance thresholds, leakage boundary, and scale decision rule.</p>
:::


<details class="hub-details">
<summary>Evidence and current knowledge</summary>
## How does it work?

- Select a deterministic stratified pilot sample and judge every candidate response pointwise against the question and provisional grounded reference.
- Apply randomized, reversal-checked pairwise judging only to the top or uncertain group.
- Audit judge quality, stability, position sensitivity, cost, and downstream development-ranking value before any scale-up.

## What do we know?

This is prospective work, not evidence that response judging improves the
registered ranking. The grounded reference is a provisional comparison pivot,
not organizer gold, and the judge must be allowed to return uncertainty. No
scale-up is justified until the bounded pilot has frozen quality, stability,
cost, leakage, and downstream-value gates.
</details>
